claim: Leukemia inhibitory factor (Lif)-activated Jak-Stat signaling controls the onset of neurogenic-to-astrogliogenic transition.
source: It is known that leukemia inhibitory factor (Lif)-activated Jak-Stat signaling controls the onset of neurogenic-to-astrogliogenic transition (Bonni et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bonni et al., 1997.

claim: Lif-activated Jak-Stat signaling pathway in neural stem/progenitor cells starts with three critical components at the cell membrane: the heterodimeric Lif receptor Lifr-beta and Il6st, as well as the receptor-associated Janus kinase (Jak).
source: Lif-activated Jak-Stat signaling pathway in neural stem/progenitor cells (NPCs) starts with three critical components at the cell membrane: the heterodimeric Lif receptor Lifr-beta and Il6st, as well as the receptor-associated Janus kinase (Jak), which are involved in activation of the signaling transducer and activator of transcription (Stat) (Sun et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2001.

claim: The expression of the proneural basic-Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) factor neurogenin 1 (Ngn1) inhibits glial differentiation by sequestering the transcription co-activators Crebbp (CBP)/E1A binding protein p300 (Ep300) away from glial specific promoters.
source: We previously demonstrated that the expression of the proneural basic-Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) factor neurogenin 1 (Ngn1) inhibits glial differentiation by two distinct mechanisms: (1) Ngn1 sequesters the transcription co-activators Crebbp (CBP)/E1A binding protein p300 (Ep300) away from glial specific promoters
evidence: The claim is based on the authors' previous work as stated in the manuscript.

claim: Ngn1 inhibits Stat1/3 phosphorylation.
source: We previously demonstrated that the expression of the proneural basic-Helix-Loop-Helix (bHLH) factor neurogenin 1 (Ngn1) inhibits glial differentiation by two distinct mechanisms: (1) Ngn1 sequesters the transcription co-activators Crebbp (CBP)/E1A binding protein p300 (Ep300) away from glial specific promoters; (2) Ngn1 inhibits Stat1/3 phosphorylation (Sun et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2001.

claim: During astrogliogenic period, phosphor-Stat1/3 directly induces the expression of Il6st and Jak1 to strengthen Stat signaling and trigger astrogliogenesis.
source: Moreover, we have previously revealed that during astrogliogenic period, phosphor-Stat1/3 directly induces the expression of Il6st and Jak1 to strengthen Stat signaling and trigger astrogliogenesis (He et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to He et al., 2005.

claim: Protein and mRNA levels of Ngn1 were high during neurogenesis (E12 to E15) but significantly reduced during astrogliogenesis (P0–P4).
source: Our previous and current studies showed that protein and mRNA levels of Ngn1 were high during neurogenesis (E12 to E15) but significantly reduced during astrogliogenesis (P0–P4) (Figure 1A, lower panel) (He et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A and a citation to He et al., 2005.

claim: Expression of miR-9 showed a bell-shaped pattern with their expression reaching maximum level at E16, right before the onset of astrogliogenesis.
source: While screening the expression pattern of brain specific miRNAs in developing brains and in adult brains by quantitative PCR (qPCR), we found that expression of miR-9 showed a bell-shaped pattern with their expression reaching maximum level at E16, right before the onset of astrogliogenesis (Figure 1A, upper panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1A, upper panel.

claim: miR-9 was extensively expressed in the ventricular zone (VZ) and subventricular zone (SVZ) progenitors in prenatal brains.
source: Our ISH data showed that miR-9 was extensively expressed in the ventricular zone (VZ) and subventricular zone (SVZ) progenitors in prenatal brains.
evidence: The claim is supported by in situ hybridization (ISH) data.

claim: In neonatal brains (P1–P7), the expression of miR-9 persisted in the SVZ, but at a lower level.
source: In neonatal brains (P1–P7), the expression of miR-9 persisted in the SVZ, but at a lower level (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Ngn1 was highly expressed in VZ/SVZ progenitors during neurogenic period.
source: Previous studies by Britz et al. (2006) and Ge et al. (2006) showed that the Ngn1 was highly expressed in VZ/SVZ progenitors during neurogenic period.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Britz et al. (2006) and Ge et al. (2006).

claim: A putative Ngn1 binding site containing the E-box element CATATG is located 2.5 kb upstream of the miR-9-2 TSS.
source: By searching upstream sequences of the transcription start sites (TSS) of all three mouse miR-9 genes, we identified a putative Ngn1 binding site containing the E-box element CATATG located 2.5 kb upstream of the miR-9-2 TSS (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ngn1, but not its DNA-binding mutant form, AQ-Ngn1, specifically activated the miR-9-2 promoter-driven luciferase reporter.
source: Subsequently, we confirmed that Ngn1, but not its DNA-binding mutant form, AQ-Ngn1, specifically activated the miR-9-2 promoter-driven luciferase reporter (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: When the E-box element was mutated, Ngn1 activation of the miR-9-2 promoter was abolished.
source: As expected, when the E-box element was mutated, Ngn1 activation of the miR-9-2 promoter was abolished (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Ngn1 directly associated with the miR-9-2 putative promoter region encompassing the E-box element, but not to the promoter of an irrelevant/control brain enriched miRNA, miR-99b.
source: The ChIP-qPCR analysis showed that Ngn1 directly associated with the miR-9-2 putative promoter region encompassing the E-box element, but not to the promoter of an irrelevant/control brain enriched miRNA, miR-99b (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The miR-9-2 promoter was occupied by endogenous Ngn1 in E15 but not in P3 cortex.
source: We found that the miR-9-2 promoter was occupied by endogenous Ngn1 in E15 but not in P3 cortex (Figure 1E).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Overexpression of Ngn1 significantly up-regulated miR-9 expression.
source: Finally, we found that overexpression of Ngn1 significantly up-regulated miR-9 expression (Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ngn1 inhibited astrogliogenesis partially by inhibiting the astrogliogenic Jak-Stat pathway.
source: Previous and current studies have showed that (1) Ngn1 inhibited astrogliogenesis partially by inhibiting the astrogliogenic Jak-Stat pathway (Sun et al., 2001)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2001.

claim: miR-9 potentially inhibited Stat activation in mouse embryonic stem cell in vitro.
source: (2) miR-9 potentially inhibited Stat activation in mouse embryonic stem cell in vitro (Krichevsky et al., 2006)
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Krichevsky et al., 2006.

claim: Overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes by using three astrocyte markers, Aldh1l1, Slc1a3 (EAAT1), and Gfap.
source: Our in vivo study showed that overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes by using three astrocyte markers, Aldh1l1, Slc1a3 (EAAT1), and Gfap, while knockdown of miR-9 increased it (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Knockdown of miR-9 increased the number of astrocytes.
source: Our in vivo study showed that overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes by using three astrocyte markers, Aldh1l1, Slc1a3 (EAAT1), and Gfap, while knockdown of miR-9 increased it (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: Neither overexpressing nor knocking down miR-9 had significant effect on the number of Rbfox3+ (NeuN+) neurons.
source: We found that neither overexpressing nor knocking down miR-9 had significant effect on the number of Rbfox3+ (NeuN+) neurons (Figure 2B–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B-D.

claim: miR-9 was expressed in neurons (Rbfox3+), but not in astrocytes (Gfap+).
source: By miR-9 ISH combined with Gfap and Rbfox3 immunostaining analysis in adult mouse brains, it became clear that miR-9 was expressed in neurons (Rbfox3+), but not in astrocytes (Gfap+) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B)
evidence: The claim is supported by ISH and immunostaining data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes in vitro.
source: Overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes, whereas knockdown of miR-9 had the opposite effect (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Knockdown of miR-9 increased the number of astrocytes in vitro.
source: Overexpression of miR-9 significantly decreased the number of astrocytes, whereas knockdown of miR-9 had the opposite effect (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Transfection of mouse E11 NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplexes significantly reduced the number of astrocytes, while having no significant effect on the number of neurons.
source: Transfection of mouse E11 NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplexes significantly reduced the number of astrocytes, while having no significant effect on the number of neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: miR-9 suppressed the activation of glial-specific Gfap promoter, with little effect on the neurogenic promoter Neurod1.
source: In agreement with our in vivo and in vitro findings, the luciferase reporter assays showed that miR-9 suppressed the activation of glial-specific Gfap promoter, with little effect on the neurogenic promoter Neurod1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Ngn1 could both activate the neurogenic program and simultaneously inhibit the astrogliogenic program.
source: While Ngn1 could both activate the neurogenic program and simultaneously inhibit the astrogliogenic program (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Transfection of mouse NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplex blocked phosphorylation of Stat1/3 without altering their protein levels.
source: We confirmed that transfection of mouse NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplex blocked phosphorylation of Stat1/3 without altering their protein levels (Figure 3B)
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 contain putative miR-9 binding-sites.
source: To explore how miR-9 inhibits Stat phosphorylation, we scanned the 3′ UTRs of three upstream components of the Jak-Stat pathway (www.targetscan.com) and found that Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 contain putative miR-9 binding-sites (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Transfection of exogenous miR-9 duplex led to an average of 40% decrease in luciferase activities of reporter constructs carrying 3′ UTRs of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 mRNAs.
source: Transfection of exogenous miR-9 duplex led to an average of 40% decrease in luciferase activities of reporter constructs carrying 3′ UTRs of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 mRNAs. Such effect was reversed by a miR-9 inhibitor (duplex) (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The effects of miR-9 on the targets were dependent on the miR-9 binding-sites within the 3′ UTRs as the luciferase reporter containing mutant Lifr-beta 3′ UTR (with mutated miR-9 binding-site) was resistant to miR-9 inhibition.
source: Furthermore, we showed that the effects of miR-9 on the targets were dependent on the miR-9 binding-sites within the 3′ UTRs as the luciferase reporter containing mutant Lifr-beta 3′ UTR (with mutated miR-9 binding-site) was resistant to miR-9 inhibition (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The transfection of mouse NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplex reduced protein levels of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1.
source: In line with the luciferase assay, we showed that the transfection of mouse NPCs with exogenous miR-9 duplex reduced protein levels of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Ngn1 down-regulated the expression levels of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1.
source: We confirmed that Ngn1 also down-regulated the expression levels of Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 2C) (Sun et al., 2001; He et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2C and citations to Sun et al., 2001 and He et al., 2005.

claim: Overexpression of Ngn1 suppressed the luciferase activities of all three critical component of Jak-Stat pathway.
source: We further verified this result by luciferase assays. Overexpression of Ngn1 suppressed the luciferase activities of all three critical component of Jak-Stat pathway (Figure 3—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2D.

claim: Co-expression of a constitutively active form of Stat3 (Stat3C) with miR-9 in NPCs could bypass the effect of miR-9 inhibition on astrocyte differentiation.
source: In supporting the above-mentioned findings, we showed that co-expression of a constitutively active form of Stat3 (Stat3C) with miR-9 in NPCs could bypass the effect of miR-9 inhibition on astrocyte differentiation (Figure 3E).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Jak-Stat signaling has a positive auto-regulation loop, where phosphor-Stat1/3 activates Il6st and Jak1 expression.
source: In addition, we previously showed that Jak-Stat signaling has a positive auto-regulation loop, where phosphor-Stat1/3 activates Il6st and Jak1 expression (He et al., 2005).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to He et al., 2005.

claim: Ngn1 binds to the promoter of miR-9 and activates its expression during neurogenesis.
source: Here, by employing in vivo and in vitro approaches, we report that Ngn1 binds to the promoter of a brain-enriched microRNA, miR-9, and activates its expression during neurogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches described in the manuscript including ChIP-qPCR and luciferase assays.

claim: miR-9 directly targets mRNAs of Lifr-beta, Il6st (gp130), and Jak1 to down-regulate these critical upstream components of the Jak-Stat pathway.
source: Subsequently, our in vitro study showed that miR-9 directly targets mRNAs of Lifr-beta, Il6st (gp130), and Jak1 to down-regulate these critical upstream components of the Jak-Stat pathway, achieving inhibition of Stat phosphorylation and consequently, suppression of astrogliogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by luciferase reporter assays and western blot data shown in the manuscript.

claim: miR-9 achieves inhibition of Stat phosphorylation and consequently, suppression of astrogliogenesis.
source: Subsequently, our in vitro study showed that miR-9 directly targets mRNAs of Lifr-beta, Il6st (gp130), and Jak1 to down-regulate these critical upstream components of the Jak-Stat pathway, achieving inhibition of Stat phosphorylation and consequently, suppression of astrogliogenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple experimental data including western blots and cell differentiation assays.

claim: Ngn1 modulated non-coding RNA epigenetic regulation during cell fate specifications.
source: This study revealed Ngn1 modulated non-coding RNA epigenetic regulation during cell fate specifications.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ngn1 substantially suppresses the activation of the astrogliogenic Jak-Stat pathway.
source: While Ngn1 substantially suppresses the activation of the astrogliogenic Jak-Stat pathway, the underlying molecular mechanism was unknown.
evidence: The claim is stated as established knowledge that motivated the current study.

claim: A proneural factor, neurogenin 1 (Ngn1), simultaneously activates the neurogenic program and inhibits the alternative astrogliogenic program when specifying the neuronal fate.
source: It has been postulated that a proneural factor, neurogenin 1 (Ngn1), simultaneously activates the neurogenic program and inhibits the alternative astrogliogenic program when specifying the neuronal fate.
evidence: The claim is stated as a postulate or hypothesis in the field.

claim: The expression pattern of miR-9 somewhat correlated with the expression of Ngn1, compatible with a potential regulatory relationship between Ngn1 and miR-9.
source: Taken together, these evidences implied that the expression pattern of miR-9 somewhat correlated with the expression of Ngn1, compatible with a potential regulatory relationship between Ngn1 and miR-9.
evidence: The claim is an inference drawn from the temporal expression patterns of miR-9 and Ngn1.

claim: miR-9 appeared to be only involved in the inhibition of glial fate.
source: While Ngn1 could both activate the neurogenic program and simultaneously inhibit the astrogliogenic program (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), miR-9 appeared to be only involved in the inhibition of glial fate.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the experimental data showing miR-9's effects on astrocytes but not neurons.

claim: The DNA binding mutant Ngn1 (AQ-Ngn1), by sequestration of the transcriptional co-activator Crebbp, should also inhibit Stat1/3 mediated activation of Il6st and Jak1, which in turn inhibits Stat1/3 phosphorylation.
source: Therefore, the DNA binding mutant Ngn1 (AQ-Ngn1), by sequestration of the transcriptional co-activator Crebbp, should also inhibit Stat1/3 mediated activation of Il6st and Jak1, which in turn inhibits Stat1/3 phosphorylation (Sun et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is an inference based on previous findings cited from Sun et al., 2001.

claim: The Ngn1 sequestration regulation and the Ngn1 induced miR-9 regulation acted jointly to suppress Jak-Stat signaling to warrant the neuronal cell fate specification during the time period of neurogenesis.
source: It appeared that the Ngn1 sequestration regulation and the Ngn1 induced miR-9 regulation acted jointly to suppress Jak-Stat signaling to warrant the neuronal cell fate specification during the time period of neurogenesis (Figure 3F).
evidence: The claim is a conclusion inferred from the combined experimental findings and shown in the model in Figure 3F.

claim: miRNA has emerged as a new mechanism of epigenetic regulation that can rapidly respond to extrinsic cues to pattern the activities of particular target protein-coding genes and generate different types of cells over a short period of time.
source: Since the first miRNA was discovered 20 years ago, miRNA has emerged as a new mechanism of epigenetic regulation that can rapidly respond to extrinsic cues to pattern the activities of particular target protein-coding genes and generate different types of cells over a short period of time (Lee et al., 1993; Wightman et al., 1993; Sauvageot and Stiles, 2002; Miller and Gauthier, 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to Lee et al., 1993; Wightman et al., 1993; Sauvageot and Stiles, 2002; Miller and Gauthier, 2007.

claim: miR-9 mediated the action of Ngn1 by suppressing the expression of three major components of Jak-Stat singling, Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1, which attenuated Stat1/3 phosphorylation to inhibit the astrogliogenic differentiation genes or programs.
source: This study demonstrated a novel molecular mechanism through which miR-9 mediated the action of Ngn1 by suppressing the expression of three major components of Jak-Stat singling, Lifr-beta, Il6st, and Jak1, which attenuated Stat1/3 phosphorylation to inhibit the astrogliogenic differentiation genes or programs.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ngn1 modulated multiple layers of genetic and epigenetic regulations to secure the process of neuronal fate specification.
source: Our previous and present work revealed that Ngn1 modulated multiple layers of genetic and epigenetic regulations to secure the process of neuronal fate specification.
evidence: The claim is a conclusion drawn from the current and previous work by the authors.

claim: Cells electroporated at E16 with miR-9 constructs all migrated to proper cortical layers without overt migration defects.
source: The electroporated cells (GFP+) migrated to layers 2/3 without obvious migration defect in all experimental conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by observational data from in utero electroporation experiments.

claim: Knockdown of miR-9 reduced the number of Map2+ neurons in vitro.
source: Knockdown of miR-9 reduced the number of Map2+ neurons.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.
